title: fix(objectql): the autonumber fallback reads the declared `{0000}` default instead of parsing the empty string (#7262)
body:
Closes #7262. Part of #6555 — this is the **last** of its three halves, so #6555 closes on this merge.

Execution half 2/3 of the maintainer's route-3 ruling. The spec half landed the contract (#7265, `88154bee1`), the driver half read it (#7263 → PR #7334), and this one takes the engine's hand-written fallback out.

## Premise check — verified on `origin/main` @ `8a857a22b`

| the card claims | measured | verdict |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `resolveAutonumberFormat` / `DEFAULT_AUTONUMBER_FORMAT` live in `@objectstack/spec/data` | `packages/spec/src/data/autonumber-format.ts:167` and `:196`; public via `api-surface/data.json` | ✅ blocker discharged |
| `engine.ts` already imports from that entry | `engine.ts:28` — one symbol added, no new dependency | ✅ |
| the two-line hand fallback is still there | `engine.ts:2654-2655`, verbatim as quoted (the card's `:2553` had drifted) | ✅ |
| a format-less field renders bare on this path | probed both readings directly: old ⇒ `1` / `11`, new ⇒ `0001` / `0011` | ✅ |
| `''` moves too (`??` → truthiness) | old `''` ⇒ bare; new ⇒ `{0000}`. Also measured a case the card does not name — see move 2 below | ✅ + one addition |
| the fallback-path doc table at `:2700` documents the bare-integer emission | that table (now `:2801`) is the **driver-capability / collision-resync** table — which drivers take the fallback path and how a duplicate surfaces. It documents neither rendering nor bare integers, and this change does not move any cell in it | ⚠️ reported, not manufactured — see "Documentation" |

## The change

`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, `applyAutonumbers`:

```ts
-const fmt = (def as any).autonumberFormat ?? (def as any).format;
-const tokens = parseAutonumberFormat(typeof fmt === 'string' ? fmt : '');
+const fmt = resolveAutonumberFormat(def as never);
+const tokens = parseAutonumberFormat(fmt);
```

One deviation from the card's one-liner: `fmt` is kept as a binding because the empty-`{field}` refusal below it interpolates the format into its message. Folding the call into `parseAutonumberFormat(...)` alone would not compile. Side effect, an improvement: that diagnostic now names the format actually rendered with instead of `undefined`.

## Two behaviour moves — this half is not neutral

**1. A format-less field on the engine fallback path issues `0001` where it issued `1`.** The path is taken whenever the driver does not advertise `supports.autonumber` (`driver-memory`, `driver-mongodb`, any driver without the capability). The ruling's compatibility note, verbatim:

> Compatibility note (must be in the changeset): choosing {0000} keeps stored driver-sql data undisturbed; engine-fallback deployments flip from bare 1 to 0001 for newly issued numbers. Counter continuity itself is unaffected (#6468 pinned it).

Counter continuity is genuinely untouched, and measurably so: `{0000}` renders prefix `''` and suffix `''`, so `readStoredAutonumberCounter` stays on its **unanchored** legacy branch and goes on reading already-stored bare values (`1`, `2`, `10` ⇒ next counter 11, now rendered `0011`). Only the width of newly issued numbers moves.

**2. An EMPTY declared format is now "undeclared".** `??` respects an empty string; the resolver's rule is non-empty-string, which is driver-sql's long-standing one and is what makes the two sides agree. So `autonumberFormat: ''` and `format: ''` resolve to `{0000}` instead of rendering bare.

**2b — an addition the card does not name, found while writing the case for it.** The same rule change has a second, sharper edge: `'' ?? 'D-{0000}'` is `''` (nullish coalescing does not fall through an empty string), so an empty canonical key used to **mask a declared shorthand** entirely and render bare. It now falls through: `{ autonumberFormat: '', format: 'D-{0000}' }` renders `D-0001`. Pinned as its own case and written into the changeset.

The escape hatch for anyone who wants an unpadded number is unchanged and documented: declare a format with no `{0..0}` slot (`'PRE-'` → `PRE-1`). `autonumberFormat: ''` is not that spelling.

## The measured coverage gap this closes

The drivers seat measured (#7262 comment 5237739551) that **no test on either side declared an empty-string format** — 0 of 8 driver-sql autonumber suites, 0 of 7 `engine-autonumber-*` suites — while `''` is exactly the input this half moves. New `packages/objectql/src/engine-autonumber-default-format.test.ts` is written for that gap: 7 cases on the moving legs (format-less on an empty store, the `1`/`2`/`10` reproduction, counter continuity across calls, `autonumberFormat: ''`, `format: ''`, the empty-canonical-masks-shorthand edge, a non-string key) and 4 explicitly-labelled controls for the surface that must not move (a declared format honoured as written, canonical-over-shorthand precedence, the slot-less escape hatch, and a driver owning autonumber being untouched).

`packages/runtime/src/autonumber-seed-cross-side-parity.integration.test.ts` gains the bug report's own reproduction as a fifth fixture — **no format declared**, stored `1`/`2`/`10`, both real implementations, `0011`. Every pre-existing fixture there declares a format, so all four agreed on width by construction; this is the one that did not, and it is what makes that file assert a shared **rendering** rather than only a shared counter.

## Re-pinned tests — every one, as required

Five pre-existing cases asserted the defect (a bare number on a format-less field). Each is re-pinned to the padded form with a comment naming #6555 so it is not "fixed" back.

| file | case | was | now |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `objectql/src/engine-autonumber-seed-suffix.test.ts` | reads the LAST digit run of the whole value | `'11'` | `'0011'` |
| `objectql/src/engine-autonumber-seed-suffix.test.ts` | reads past leading text that no format describes | `'8'` | `'0008'` |
| `objectql/src/engine-autonumber-seed-scan.test.ts` | takes the NUMERIC max, not the lexicographic one | `'11'` (+ `not.toBe('10')`) | `'0011'` (+ `not.toBe('0010')`) |
| `objectql/src/engine-insert-runtime-owned-strip.test.ts` | #5503 UNCHANGED: a caller seed that NO hook overwrote is still stripped | `'1'` | `'0001'` |
| `objectql/src/engine-insert-runtime-owned-strip.test.ts` | BULK: one batch, mixed rows | `'1'` / `'2'` | `'0001'` / `'0002'` |

Two more touched but **not** re-pinnings, called out so the list is not read as complete-by-luck:

- `engine-insert-runtime-owned-strip.test.ts` case B holds `expect(row.code).not.toBe('1')` and the value under test is `'HOOK-B'`, so it passes either way. Moved to `'0001'` because the fix silently **weakens** it — `'1'` stopped being the sequence value the guard means to exclude. A guard-strength restoration, not a behaviour pin.
- `driver-sql/src/sql-driver-autonumber-suffix.test.ts` — prose only, no assertion touched. The driver half wrote there that "the engine's fallback still emits the bare `11` until #7262 lands the other half"; this PR is what makes that false. The driver half edited the same comment for the same reason, so this is its follow-through, not a scope excursion. All 59 driver-sql autonumber tests stay green unedited.

## Reverse verification — predicted in writing before running

Procedure: keep every test edit, remove the fix with `git checkout origin/main -- packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, re-run, restore. Never `git stash`.

| # | prediction | measured |
|:---|:---|:---|
| 1 | new suite's moving cases red | **7 red** — I enumerated 6 and wrote 7; the extra ("the counter continues across calls") was a case I wrote but did not list separately. Reported rather than back-fitted |
| 2 | `engine-autonumber-seed-suffix.test.ts` 2 red | **2 red** ✅ |
| 3 | `engine-autonumber-seed-scan.test.ts` 1 red | **1 red** ✅ |
| 4 | runtime parity fixture red, engine `11` vs SQL `0011` | **1 red**, `expected '11' to be '0011'` ✅ — the only case in that file whose arms may disagree today |
| 5 | new suite's 4 controls green in both directions | **green both ways** ✅ — stated so a green run is not misread as coverage for the moving leg |
| 6 | `seed-scan`'s 6000-row walk blind to the change | **green both ways** ✅ — it issues 6001, and `padStart(4,'0')` of 6001 is `6001`; padded and bare are byte-identical past 4 digits. Left untouched rather than "re-pinned" |
| 7 | `insert-runtime-owned-strip` case B green both ways | **green both ways** ✅ |
| — | *(not predicted)* | **2 extra red** in `insert-runtime-owned-strip.test.ts`: the `#5503 UNCHANGED` and `BULK` cases assert bare `'1'`/`'2'` positively. The prediction was written before I had found them; a full-package run did, and they are rows 4–5 of the re-pin table. An honest miss in the enumeration, not in the outcome |

Totals with the fix removed: **12 red** in `packages/objectql`, **1 red** in `packages/runtime`, driver-sql and spec green.

**Methodology note worth carrying forward.** The runtime parity arm resolves `@objectstack/objectql` through its built `dist`, so the first reverse-verification run of it passed with the source reverted — the revert had not reached the artefact under test. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql build` between the revert and the run is what makes that arm honest. Same shape as AGENTS.md §9's stale-artefact trap, in mirror image.

## Documentation

The `applyAutonumbers` docstring claimed the fallback behaves "identically to the SQL driver's persistent sequence (#1603)" — true of every declared format and false of the one case nobody declares, which is the whole defect. It now carries a `#6555` section stating the two moves, the `{0000}` choice, the escape hatch, and why seeding is unaffected.

The table the triage pointed at (`:2700` then, `:2801` now) is reported above rather than edited: it is the driver-capability / collision-resync table, and this change moves no cell in it. Editing it to fit the dispatch's expectation would have been a fabrication.

## Changeset

`.changeset/autonumber-format-defallback-engine.md` — **`@objectstack/objectql: minor`**, carrying the ruling's compatibility note verbatim plus both behaviour moves and the escape hatch.

Level justified from the siblings rather than by feel: the spec half took `minor` for adding exports, and the driver half took `patch` on an explicit neutrality argument — its own words, *"Behaviour-neutral, by construction and by measurement … This half moves neither."* Neutrality is what earned that `patch`, and this half is precisely the one that is not neutral, so it goes a level up. Not `major`: nothing authorable is removed or renamed, there is no FROM → TO migration, and `breakingDeclaration()` in `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` therefore does not judge it (no `major` bump, no `**BREAKING`, no `!` in the summary) — verified by running the gate.

## Gates — all local, all green

| gate | result |
|:---|:---|
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql test` | **173 files, 3077 tests passed** |
| `packages/runtime` cross-side parity | **6 passed** (was 5 — the new fixture) |
| `packages/drivers/driver-sql` autonumber suites | **7 files, 59 passed**, assertions unedited |
| `typecheck` — objectql, runtime, driver-sql | all `Done` |
| `eslint` on all 7 changed files | clean |
| `check:nul-bytes` | OK, 6789 files, no raw control bytes |
| `check:driver-memory-census` · `check:engine-double-contract` · `check:error-code-casing` · `check:route-envelope` · `check:empty-changeset` · `check:adr-0087-registration` · `check:spec-parsed-alias` · `check:query-options-erasure` | PASS |

`docs/adr/**` and `content/docs/releases/` untouched. No spec schema edits — none were needed.

Heavy runs serialized under `flock /tmp/os-heavy-verify.lock` with `--max-old-space-size=4096` and `--maxWorkers=2`.
